lesson.subtitle: Lesson 11 -- What Are You Doing These Days?
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Bruna Viana da Silva Rocha | Lesson 11 -- What Are You Doing These Days?

listenings.text: Two years ago I decided to take up running, and I want to be honest about how that went. I hated it. I hated getting up early, I hated the cold, and I really hated being passed by people who were twice my age. So I gave up after three weeks. What changed was not motivation. A friend suggested running at night instead, after work, when I was already tired and annoyed, and that turned out to be the secret. I stopped trying to become a morning person. I kept doing the thing I already wanted to do, which was to get out of the house and stop thinking. These days I run three times a week, and I actually look forward to it. My advice is simple. Do not ask yourself what you should enjoy. Ask yourself when you would not mind doing it, and start there.

I have been running this RV park outside Anchorage for nineteen summers, and I hear the same sentence almost every night at the fire pit. People tell me they always wanted to do this trip, and that they kept putting it off. First the kids were too small, then work got busy, then somebody needed to finish paying for the house. Most of them are in their sixties. The ones who surprise me are the young ones, the couples in their thirties who just decided to go. I asked one of them last year how they managed to stop waiting. She said they made a rule. Every time one of them said someday, the other one had to name a month. That was it. They chose June, they booked the ferry, and they spent the whole winter planning the route. So if you are thinking about coming up here, do not wait to feel ready. Pick a month. The mountains are not going anywhere, but you might.
